**Trader consensus centers on 86–87°F as the most probable high for Atlanta on August 5, 2026, at 43.5% implied probability, followed by 84–85°F at 29.5%.** This positioning reflects current National Weather Service and model guidance pointing to a typical early-August diurnal pattern of morning sunshine followed by scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms, which often limits peak heating through increased cloud cover and evaporative cooling.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Pakistan Meteorological Department and AccuWeather place Karachi's daily maximum temperatures in the 31–35°C range during early August 2026, with the August average high near 33°C amid the southwest monsoon. Partly cloudy conditions and scattered rainfall expected over the next 48 hours favor 32–34°C peaks by suppressing full insolation while maintaining high humidity and limited sea-breeze moderation. Model consensus shows no heatwave signals or extreme ridging, keeping probabilities concentrated on 33°C as the mode, with 32°C and 34°C reflecting minor day-to-day variability from cloud timing and wind shifts. Historical August climatology supports this narrow band, and the market-implied odds align closely with the latest ensemble guidance ahead of final observational data on August 6.
